subject: Re: Plan re-tiering + feature bundle options for CareSense pilot
messages:
From: Jorge Ramos <jorge@caresense.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@caresense.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Plan options for pilot -> scale (CareSense)

Michael —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re moving quickly on the pilot approval and Procurement has two asks before we circulate for finance: 1) can you outline the clean upgrade path if we exceed the pilot throughput (we expect bursty traffic), and 2) are there bundling options that reduce unit cost for embeddings vs generation? They also attached the RFP so you can see current usage assumptions.

High level constraints:
- Pilot: 3 months, expect 3 small models + embeddings for search.
- Goal: grow to 10 models in 12 months with periodic bursts (holiday windows).
- Security: standard SOC2 request (Procurement will follow up separately).

Can you send a short note showing 2 upgrade scenarios (conservative vs aggressive) and a simple comparison of bundling (seat/throughput vs per-token) so I can share internally?

Appreciate it — aim to get this into the packet by end of next week.

Best,
Jorge Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering
CareSense

Attachment: CareSense_RFP_May2028.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge@caresense.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Plan options for pilot -> scale (CareSense)

Jorge —

Thanks for the clear asks and the RFP. Quick summary below, I’ve attached a compact pricing sheet with two scenario sketches and recommended bundling. Short version up front: we can offer a staged upgrade path with predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated) at the 6-month mark and an embedding-heavy bundle that materially lowers unit cost for embeddings.

Conservative scenario (pilot-first):
- Months 0–3 (pilot): Hosted API, capped throughput, per-token billing.
- Months 4–6: Move to Dedicated reserved pool (small) once steady throughput > 200k tokens/day sustained for a week.
- 6–12 months: Scale Dedicated via add-on throughput (slots) and enable prefix caching for the search model to cut token cost ~25%.

Aggressive scenario (fast scale):
- Months 0–1: Pilot on Hosted with burst rules.
- Month 2: Commit to Dedicated medium pool with burst buffer for holiday windows.
- Month 3–12: Add a quantized model variant for generation (lower cost), plus a bundled embedding package (fixed monthly embedding units).

Bundling recommendation (embeddings-heavy):
- Option A: Hybrid bundle — monthly embedding units + per-token generation. Embedding unit bucket priced ~40% below hosted per-unit when paired with a 12-month commit.
- Option B: Throughput-first bundle — reserved GPU slots + unlimited low-rate embeddings (for high-search workloads). Best for predictable, high-QPS search.

Concessions we can consider for this deal: one-time pilot credit (covers up to $20k of usage) and a two-month discounted rate on Dedicated setup if they sign a 12-month commitment. Ben — I’ve left the pricing suggestions in the attached redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx, can you confirm the margin impact and a recommended discount cap?

Next steps:
- I can create a one-page mutual action plan for Procurement to include in the packet.
- If useful, we can set a short call with Procurement to walk through the SOC2 evidence and the upgrade mechanics.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)

Michael / Lauren —

Quick checks on the numbers in the spreadsheet:
- Embedding bundle at 12-month commit: can go as low as 35% below hosted list but that requires a minimum monthly embedding unit floor (we used 1.2M units/mo in the calc).
- Dedicated setup discount: I recommend capping the onboarding credit at $15k for pilot conversion; larger credits should be tied to a minimum 9–12 month revenue commit.
- Holiday/burst buffer: suggest adding a "burst cap" clause (X% over commit for up to Y hours per month) — avoids surprise overage conversations and preserves SLOs.

If Jorge wants a true conservative proposal, include both the per-token hosted vs hybrid bundle cost comparison for the first 12 months (I added a two-column view in the sheet).

Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

- If they choose the embedding-heavy bundle, we’ll include an embedding floor and a 12-month price lock.
